title: Linux.Mirai_Incident_Response_e88
description: Investigate and respond to a potential compromise on a victim host exhibiting unusual behavior.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has exhibited unusual behavior, including unexpected outbound network connections and suspicious scheduled tasks. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential compromise.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Scheduled Tasks
levels.content: Investigate the suspicious scheduled tasks on the victim host. Identify and investigate any unauthorized or suspicious scheduled tasks that may be responsible for automatically executing malware. Check systemd timers and services for the 'network-diagnostics.timer'.
levels.solution: Check the systemd timers and services on the victim host. Look for any suspicious or unauthorized tasks that may be related to the malware.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd timers and services on the victim host.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any suspicious or unauthorized tasks.

levels.title: Locate Files Installed by the Malware
levels.content: Locate files installed by the malware on the compromised host. Correlate suspicious activity with files introduced by the trojan. Investigate hidden or unusual filesystem locations such as '/usr/local/lib/.netd/revshell.sh'.
levels.solution: Investigate hidden or unusual filesystem locations used by the trojan. Look for files in directories like /usr/local/lib/.netd and /var/lib/.netd.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate hidden or unusual filesystem locations used by the trojan.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for files in directories like /usr/local/lib/.netd.

levels.title: Determine the External Host Communicating with the Compromised System
levels.content: Determine the external host communicating with the compromised system. Analyze network connections and identify the command-and-control server. Check for connections to '192.168.60.20'.
levels.solution: Check the network connections and logs on the victim host. Look for any suspicious outbound connections to external hosts.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the network connections and logs on the victim host.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any suspicious outbound connections to external hosts.
